title: eunox Config
description: Configuration for `eunox proxy --config <file>`. The top-level `transport` selects the host-facing transport: "http" (default, gateway shape) fronts many MCP upstreams from one process, each on its own /mcp/<name> route; "stdio" speaks MCP over stdin/stdout to exactly one upstream. Each upstream is governed by its own capability manifest, all writing to one shared, signed audit tape. Connection wiring lives here; enforcement policy stays in the per-route manifest files referenced by `policy`.

schemaVersion.description: Config grammar version. Required. This build understands "0.1"; a document with an absent or unrecognized value is rejected at load (fail-closed). Distinct from a manifest's policy-content version.

transport.description: Host-facing transport — how eunox speaks to its MCP host. "http" (default) listens on a socket and fronts N upstreams on /mcp/<name> routes. "stdio" speaks MCP over stdin/stdout to exactly one upstream (no `listen` block). "" (or an omitted key) defaults to "http". Independent of each upstream's own `transport`.

listen.description: Where the gateway binds for incoming MCP hosts.

bind.description: Bind address. Defaults to 127.0.0.1. Binding to a non-loopback address additionally requires the --unsafe-bind-all CLI flag.

port.description: TCP port to listen on. 0 (or an omitted key) means unset — the loader applies the default 3000. A non-zero value must be in [1, 65535].

authToken.description: Optional static bearer token required from incoming hosts (Authorization: Bearer <token>). Use ${VAR} to read it from the environment rather than committing it. A literal $ that is not a valid reference, and any reference to an unset variable, are left untouched — so a token containing $ is never blanked or corrupted.

oauthResource.description: URI identifying this resource server (RFC 9728 'resource' field). When set, published in the protected-resource metadata document at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and in WWW-Authenticate challenges as resource_metadata. Never derived from the request Host header. Only valid for transport: http.

oauthAuthorizationServers.description: Authorization server URIs published in the RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata document. Defaults to --jwt-issuer when not set. Only valid for transport: http.

allowedOrigins.description: Extends the built-in Origin allowlist (loopback names and the bind host) used by the DNS-rebinding guard. List full origins, e.g. "https://app.example.com". A present Origin header that matches none of the allowed origins is rejected with 403. Only valid for transport: http.

trustedProxyCIDRs.description: CIDR ranges a reverse proxy may connect from for its X-Forwarded-For header to be trusted under --trust-forwarded-for. The immediate TCP peer must match one of these ranges, or X-Forwarded-For is ignored and the connection's own address is used instead. Only valid for transport: http.

trustedProxyHops.description: How many trusted reverse proxies sit in front of eunox. Each hop appends the address it saw to X-Forwarded-For, so the right-most N entries are proxy-written and the client's real address is the N-th from the right; entries further left are client-supplied and ignored. Defaults to 1 (a single proxy, i.e. the right-most entry). Declare the real chain depth rather than relying on trustedProxyCIDRs to identify hops: an entry inside that range is indistinguishable from a client whose own address falls in it. Only valid for transport: http.

maxSessions.description: Cap on concurrent client sessions; each session owns one upstream subprocess or remote connection. A new initialize beyond the cap is refused with 503 rather than spawning unbounded upstreams. 0 means unlimited. When this key is omitted, the proxy applies a safe backstop default (see --max-sessions). Only valid for transport: http.

sessionIdleTimeoutMs.description: Reap a session whose host has sent no request for this many milliseconds, closing its upstream so idle sessions cannot pin resources. 0 (default) disables idle reaping. Only valid for transport: http.

audit.description: Shared OCSF audit tape for every route. Each record is signed with HMAC-SHA256 and stamped with the handling upstream, the in-force policy version, and a policy digest.

log.description: Path to the append-only audit log (JSON Lines). Defaults to ~/.eunox/audit.jsonl.

keyPath.description: Path to the HMAC signing key. Generated with mode 0600 on first run if absent. Defaults to ~/.eunox/audit.key.

rotateSizeBytes.description: Rotate the audit log once it exceeds this size, in bytes. Defaults to 104857600 (100 MiB). 0 (default) uses the built-in size; a negative value is rejected at load.

retainRotated.description: Bound how many rotated audit files (audit.jsonl.<timestamp>) are kept after each rotation; the oldest beyond this count are deleted so the log directory cannot grow without bound. 0 (default) keeps every rotated file. The active log is never deleted.

upstreams.description: One entry per upstream MCP server. With transport: http each is served at POST /mcp/<name>; with transport: stdio there is exactly one.

then.description: transport: stdio has no network listener and fronts exactly one upstream.

routeDefaults.description: Enforcement posture applied to every route unless overridden per-upstream.

enforcement.description: Enforcement posture applied to every route: "enforce" (default — block on denial) or "audit" (observe — evaluate and log, but forward instead of block). "" (or an omitted key) defaults to "enforce".

strictDrift.description: Treat any manifest/upstream capability drift as fatal rather than warning.

taskAnchoredState.description: Key accumulated enforcement state — flow-label taint, sequenceBlock antecedents, maxCalls and cumulative blastRadius budgets, spent single-use declassify grants — on the caller's VALIDATED mcp.task_id claim rather than on its session, so the state survives a hop between enforcement points instead of restarting clean on the far side. Off by default because it changes what every budget in a policy MEANS: a maxCalls of 20 becomes 20 per task rather than 20 per connection. A request with no token at all is anchored on its session exactly as it is today, so this can never make two unauthenticated callers share state; a request that presented a token carrying no task_id is DENIED (MISSING_CONTEXT) rather than accounted against a second, session-keyed bucket. It does nothing without a JWT integration that mints mcp.task_id.

upstreamTimeoutMs.description: Per-call timeout when contacting an upstream, in milliseconds. The loader treats a value of 0 as unset (the flag/default applies) and rejects a negative value; the maximum guards against overflow when the value is scaled to nanoseconds.

upstream.description: One upstream route. transport selects the wiring: 'stdio' launches `command` as a subprocess; 'http' proxies to `upstreamUrl`.

name.description: Route name, used verbatim as the /mcp/<name> URL path segment. Must be unique across upstreams.

command.description: stdio transport only: executable to launch as the upstream MCP server subprocess.

args.description: stdio transport only: arguments passed to `command`.

upstreamUrl.description: http transport only: base URL of the upstream MCP server.

upstreamAuthHeader.description: http transport only: a header line injected on every upstream request, e.g. 'Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}'. Use ${VAR} to avoid committing secrets; ${VAR}/$VAR are expanded from the environment, and a literal $ or a reference to an unset variable is left untouched.

upstreamTlsSkipVerify.description: http transport only: skip TLS certificate verification for the upstream. For local/dev use only.

policy.description: One or more capability manifest files, merged in order, governing this route. Omitting it is only valid when the effective enforcement is "audit" (observe-only): in gateway mode a route with no policy and no audit posture fails closed at startup (the gateway refuses to start). With "audit", the route forwards and logs every call without blocking.

expectVersion.description: Pin the manifest's `version`. When set and the loaded version differs, the gateway fails closed (refuses to start). Requires `policy` to be set, and is only supported with a single policy file (the pin is unambiguous only then).

enforcement.description: Per-route enforcement posture: "enforce" or "audit". "" (or an omitted key) inherits from defaults.

effectReceiptKeys.description: Path to a local JWKS document holding THIS upstream's receipt-signing public keys, enabling verification of the signed effect receipts it publishes in a tool result's `_meta` (`io.eunolabs.effect-receipt`). A distinct key domain from the caller-authenticating JWKS on purpose: a receipt is a server's statement about its own behavior, so tying it to the token issuer that authenticates callers would let anyone who can mint a caller token also mint attestations about a server. Read once from disk at startup — never fetched — and omitting it disables receipt handling entirely for the route.

then.description: stdio routes allow command/args; HTTP-only fields are rejected.
http routes allow upstreamUrl/HTTP options; stdio-only command/args are rejected.
